title: Quick review snapshots — personal scratchpad
body:
Purpose: rapid-pass personal notes after reading PRs and doing small local runs. Not polished — meant to seed future follow-ups and quick fixes.

Top-level takeaways:
- PR changes the KV-cache eviction heuristics (hotness scoring) and touches request routing. High churn surface: cadence of cache flush + route fallback.
- Tests added for canonical path, but missing concurrency/strain scenarios (small windows where two requests race to refresh).
- Nicely isolated helpers (cache/hotness), can extract a tiny experiential test harness.

Micro-checklist (fast pass, 5–10 min):
- [ ] Does new code add synchronous work on hot path? (scan for loop + network calls inside handler) — found `maybe_prefetch()` called from `serve_token()`; prefetch kicks off inline.
- [ ] Are locks held across async await boundaries? — there is `with self.lock:` before `await db.get()` in an edge case. Flag.
- [ ] Are metrics emitted on both happy/failure paths? — cache miss metric exists, but miss-type (stale vs absent) not instrumented.
- [ ] Small perf regression check: run unit `tests/test_kv_cache.py::test_hotness_decay` locally with `-k decay` for quick signal.

Refactorable spots (ideas for follow-up PRs):
1) Split hotness scoring into `score` + `policy` layers. Right now everything in `kv_cache.py` ~420 LOC; extract `policy.py` with public API `class Policy: def score(hit_count, last_access): ...` so we can A/B policies.
2) Short-circuit path for sequence-length==1 requests. Handler currently calls full pipeline even when TTL should suffice; add `fast_path` that returns cached prefix if `sequence_len <= 1` and `kv.has_prefix(req.prefix)` -> will save ~10–15% latency on microbench.
3) Small lint: several files use `time.time()` for monotonic intervals; replace with `time.monotonic()` to avoid clock jumps.
4) Move `Metric.increment("cache.eviction")` out of finally into the eviction function to avoid double-counts when exceptions bubble.

Risk notes / red flags:
- Concurrency: `cache.repopulate()` spawns background task but does not set a failure flag; if task errors, no retry/backoff exists. Could silently drop capacity.
- Fallback policy: routing fallback chain will escalate to a larger model variant; no circuit-breaker for repeated fallbacks causing cost spikes. Add health counter/limit.
- Compatibility: new serialization format for cached values uses `v2` tag but decoder still accepts only `v1`. Backwards compat bug potential on deployments with mixed runners.

Testing & reproducibility:
- Local repro steps: checkout branch, run `pytest tests/test_kv_cache.py::test_race_prefetch -k race -q` under `PYTHONWARNINGS=default` to surface awaited-deadlock warnings.
- Add small concurrency test: spawn 16 threads hitting same prefix concurrently and assert at most one DB write. Use `pytest.mark.timeout(5)` to keep CI cheap.
- Perf microbenchmark: `python -m perf run bench/kv_hit_latency.py --iters 1000` (already exists but needs adapt for new policy)

Small experiments to try (cheap):
- A: Soft TTL extension: on hit with score>threshold, extend TTL by 10% instead of full repopulate. Measure token latency 1k sample.
- B: Prefetch offload to dedicated IO worker pool (3 threads) instead of inline spawn — removes GC pressure on event loop.
- C: Hybrid in-memory bloom filter for quick existence checks to avoid DB roundtrips for obvious misses.

Concrete follow-ups (next PRs / tasks):
- PR-1: Fix lock-across-await (urgent) — minimal patch to release before `await db.get()`. Target: patch + one unit test. Owner: Silas. ETA: 2d.
- PR-2: Extract `policy.py` and wire a plugin interface; preserve existing behavior under feature-flag. Owner: Ananya. ETA: 1w.
- PR-3: Add fallback circuit-breaker for routing to model variants, telemetry + alert. Owner: Rory. ETA: 2w.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Quick grep tokens: `rg "maybe_prefetch|repopulate|hotness"` showed 7 occurrences across `kv_cache.py`, `router.py`, `bench/` — annotate them before changing.
- Check GH comment thread on PR 4231 — earlier discussion about `prefetch` being too eager. Reconcile with new commits.

Mini code snippets (for discussion / copy into PR):
- Example of guarding await with lock release:
```
# BAD
with self.lock:
    await db.get(k)
# GOOD
with self.lock:
    local_state = self._snapshot()
# release
await db.get(k, state=local_state)
```
- Backpressure sketch for fallback breaker (pseudocode):
```
if fallback_count > 5 in last_minute:
    short_circuit_to_cached_small_variant()
else:
    route_normally()
```

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should evicted entries be serialized immediately to S3 (costy) or just rely on eventual repopulate? Tradeoff: latency vs storage costs.
- How aggressive should prefetch be for short sequences? (~2x predicted next-token probability threshold) — need data.

Action items (today):
- Run `test_race_prefetch` locally and push minimal fix if reproduces.
- Add TODO comments in `kv_cache.py` marking release-prone lines.
- Draft PR description template focusing on user-visible regressions and telemetry additions.

Random thought: if we can attach a very tiny canary (1% traffic) to the new policy that logs only aggregated counters (not payload) we could run experiments safer. Add to roadmap notes.

End of scratchpad.

(If I come back to this later: convert checklist items to GH issues, tag with `infra-critical` where appropriate.)
